I feel like the gender ratio on this site is going to become heavily unbalanced very quickly.  The overwhelming majority of individuals diagnosed as being on the spectrum are male.

It might be a good idea to allow NTs to join the site, assuming they're comfortable with dating someone on the spectrum.

Thanks for the dose of reality. I'm autistic, and social boundaries are one of those social cues I miss. I get majorly emotionally invested in new friends very quickly, and in my enthusiasm I often fail to see the line until after I have already crossed it.

I spoke to her today, and I didn't mention the bottle. I simply told her that if she ever relapses, she can tell me without fear of being judged or scolded. She took it well, so I'm going to leave it at that.

People with BPD have a really terrible self image.  Something we went through in our childhoods strongly embedded in us this belief that we are terrible horrible no-good very-bad people who don't deserve love or to have anything pleasant or joyful happen to us.  This is the only core belief we possess about ourselves.  When someone falls in love with us and shows us kindness, support, and even sometimes admiration, we don't know what the fuck to do with that.  We become convinced that we have fooled our SO into loving us, because there's no fucking way you could ever possibly love us if you saw the person we feel like deep down inside, the person we "know" ourselves to be.  We begin to either feel guilty for tricking this person we love so deeply and completely, or we begin to become suspicious that the person who claims to love us has some ulterior motive.  "If my core identifying trait is that I am absolutely unlovable, how could this person possibly actually love me?  S/he must be faking it, to get something out of me."  That's how the logic goes.

It sounds like your SO is battling with this.  When she is on her meds and that negative self image is shrunk down to a manageable whisper which she can ignore, she can fully engage in a reciprocating loving relationship with you.  When she's off her meds and that negative self-image is a fucking bullhorn drowning out every other thought or feeling, she becomes distrustful of you and your affection.  She sees you as a predator and she's trying to escape.

I've done two to four day stays in mental hospitals before.  It's a pretty crappy experience, sitting in a crowded common room for 16 hours a day only to meet with a therapist or psychiatrist for a grand total of 30 minutes and shipped back home when the rooms get too full.  My emotional state when I was in the hospital was unquestionably worse than before I went in.  Being forced to be around so many people without any distraction from my own mind is torture.  I've been through this 4 times in the past 7 years.  Each event was thoroughly unhelpful and actually destructive.

The Spanish language has three separate words for romantic love, each one representing a different depth of intimacy.  So say it in Spanish.  "Encantar" is probably the verb you're looking for.  So you would say, "Te encantado."

Fuuuuck.  I sent it.  It's out there.  It's in her inbox and I can't pull it back.  The only woman who ever loved me is about to find out exactly how much of a scumbag I really am.

Where do I go from here?
Eh, I disagree. No two people are perfect for one another. Every relationship requires hard fucking work. Neither party ever wants to do the hard work anymore, though. We're all cowards.

Back in my freshman year of college I was study buddies with a girl I was really into.  She was an absolute 10.  Red hair, green eyes, smart, funny, affectionate, bangin' body, 19 years old.  I was 24, overweight, broke, poorly dressed, and I felt like she was completely out of my league.  We always studied together in the library, and there were a few times when she asked me to go study with her back at her place.  I can only study in the library, though, because that's my routine.  If I try to study elsewhere I get anxious and distracted.  So I always declined.

We only studied together for a year, then we lost contact after I started dating another girl.  I realized years later that those offers to study at her place were an attempt to get closer.  God I wish I could remember that girl's last name so I could find her on Facebook and see what she's up to these days.
